newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision says both bids high quality.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision says both bids high quality.

text.p: Spain's Retevision said on Friday that both bids for its privatisation, which was awarded to the consortium led by Spanish electricity firm Endesa and Italian telecom operator Stet, had been of high quality.
Retevision, which has a licence to be Spain's second telephone operator after Telefonica de Espana , said in a statement that the Endesa/Stet bid had earned 915.94 out of a possible 1,000 points.
The bid presented by Opera, a group made up of Spanish bank BCH, France Telecom and U.S. operator Sprint, earned 840.80 points.

"Therefore, the Board of Directors has decided to award the 60 percent of the capital of Retevision SA to the group led by Endesa and Stet for an amount of 116 billion pesetas ($783.5 million)," Retevision said in a statement.
Retevision chairman Pedro de Torres notified both participants of the decision and thanked them, recognising the "outstanding technical and economic quality of both proposals".

The distribution of points was decided by a Contracts Committee made up of representatives from the economic and development ministries as well as from Retevision, and with the assessment of Lehman Brothers investment house.
